Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt

many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

name: arc-copy-pattern-between-markers
description: Use when ARC grids contain two 5 markers and a colored motif around one. Copy the motif to the isolated marker.
---

# Copy a motif between 5 markers

Use this when a grid contains two cells colored 5, with one embedded in or directly associated with a multi-color pattern and the other isolated.

1. Treat the 5 embedded in the motif as its anchor. Record every nonzero motif cell by its row/column offset from that anchor, including cells both above/below and left/right. Do not include the anchor 5 itself as part of the copied colored motif.
2. Locate the isolated 5. Translate the motif's offsets so they are relative to this target anchor; preserve colors and exact relative geometry.
3. Keep the source motif and its anchor unchanged. At the target, replace the isolated 5 with 0, then draw the translated motif. The target anchor remains empty unless the motif itself specifies a color there.
4. Preserve the original grid dimensions and all unrelated cells. Verify no translated cells fall outside the grid and check the orientation/offsets carefully.

A demonstrated case had the source motif around a 5 near the lower edge and an isolated 5 higher in the grid; the motif was copied to the isolated marker while the source remained intact. The target 5 was erased. Treat this as a rule to test against the current instance, not an unconditional assumption if the arrangement differs.",
